recipes.name: Easy Marinated Artichokes
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste
1 (14 ounce) can quartered artichoke hearts, drained

steps.text: Combine lemon juice, oil, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper in a jar. Seal the jar and shake until oil and lemon juice emulsify.
Remove the lid and add artichoke hearts. Seal again and shake until artichoke hearts are completely coated.
Serve immediately, or if you like them cold, chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Marinated Artichokes
raw_recipe.description: Homemade marinated artichoke hearts are simple to prepare and much more affordable than the store-bought version. They're perfect for an artichoke salad!

review.reviewBody: A-W-E-S-O-M-E!!!! I used about 3/4 tsp. each salt and pepper, and that seemed to be perfect for us. I was a bit leary of the Italian seasoning, but it really gives them good flavor. I did use the optional garlic, which is a must, IMO. Be sure to use a good extra virgin olive oil. I've been eating them straight out of the fridge, but plan to make a salad w/ them for dinner, if they last that long, lol. These would also be great on an anti-pasto platter, which is what I will do w/ them next time. I think a great twist would be to add maybe 1/4-1/2 teaspoon of crushed pepper flakes in there as well...believe me, they are wonderful as is, just thinking out loud, lol. Note that these do not taste like the jarred ones @ the store...they are different, but better! This is a definite keeper that I will make often~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

I made this for an addition to a charcuterie tray for a brunch. Didn't make enough. Now, the brunch ladies just ask for a full tray of them from now on.
I won't buy the expensive marinated jars anymore. No need. These are so easy and way better.
For the tray, I purchased whole chokes and cut them in half. Then I roasted the marinated chokes @ 425 degrees to put a char on them. I watched them until they were just right. Doesn't take long.
It's now a regular staple in our home. We now purchase 28 oz. cans of chokes each week. I halve them, marinate them, roast them, then return to the marinate and refrigerate. We snack on them daily or use as sides with with almost anything. 
Thanks for this recipe. It is perfect.

My artichokes tasted better than pre-marinaded ones. On the suggestion of some of the readers, I added more olive oil and some water and used about half of the Italian seasoning, lemon, salt & pepper. It came out perfect! Thank you!
Added garlic and a little white wine to the jars. The marinade is delicious. They are in the fridge. Can’t wait to try them!

This recipe is a gem!! I couldn't believe how it easy it was to make, but how delicious it came out. 

The only thing I changed was I did not add the lemon juice because I was out. In its place I added 3 Tablespoons of red wine vinegar. 

When I woke up this morning to "taste test" them, needless to say, I almost ate them all. It is supposed to be my lunch lol.

Loved it! I question the sodium in this recipe ... since I used artichoke hearts in water rather than brine, I expect that would result in a lot less sodium. I also added a few chili flakes for extra zip! Definitely what we call ‘a do-over’.
So good. The flavors really even out and become best after marinating for 5 days. I doubled the recipe and it fit well into a Ball jar.

Simple and delicious base recipe that can be customized to taste. For my purposes for a 14oz can of quartered artichokes, I halved all of the other ingredients and it worked out just great with wonderful, bold flavors. Thank you!

I am basing this review at the moment on how easy these are to make and on how gorgeous my 2 jars came out....I cant rate taste at the moment as I gave these out as Mother's Day gifts. I used 4 cans of quartered artichokes, 1 1/2 lemons, 4 tblspns of olive oil, salt and pepper, 2 tspns of Italian seasonig and 4 cloves of crushed garlic. They looked so good in the jar, just like the ones in the store. I will update my review as soon as I get the "taste" feedback I need. Thanks for a great recipe.
*5/18/12- got my first "taste" review back from my mom who raved about these artichokes. She tried them last night and said they were perfectly seasoned and tangy. At this point the artichokes have been sitting and marinating for a lil over 2 weeks. I think as they sit the will increase in flavor.*

Turned out great. My husband is on a low sodium diet so buying marinated artichokes is out of the question. I left out the salt and used frozen artichokes and it turned out great and the recipe I was making was just like when I made it with on the shelf marinated artichokes.

Meant to buy already marinated, but picked up plain hearts by accident, so went looking for a marinade. This tasted great. I added the zest from the lemon and grated the garlic - nice and zingy! Super simple and tasted fresh.

This recipe saved my salad. I needed marinated artichoke hearts, but when I took the jar from the pantry I realized they were not marinated. The changes I made was to use the zest from the lemon, as well as the juice. Because I am allergic to garlic I used 1 1/2 Tbls olive oil and 1/2 Tbls garlic infused olive oil, about 1/2 the liquid from the jar and a small pinch of red pepper flakes. It was perfect for us! Thank you very much for this tasty recipe!

These are the best I’ve ever had. I made them to go in a salad for dinner tonight, but I want to keep eating them. I added a teaspoon of Calabrian Chile paste for kick, and it’s lovely. Thank you, it’s so simple and so much better than store bought marinated artichoke hearts.
Made exactly as recipe stated. Tasted good my family liked them a lot. A little too much Italian seasoning for me. But taste was very good. Will probably make again. Thanks for the recipe
I want to use the "Marinade" of a finished store bought jar to make my own from scratch.
Tasty easy
Great recipe. Made it a dozen times or more.

To me, this tasted exactly like artichoke hearts mixed with a bottle of italian dressing. It was good, but I guess I was expecting something a little more complex. I would recommend cutting back on the salt and italian seasoning as they were a little overpowering.

Prepared exactly as recipe directed. This is better than store bought by a mile. Very good. When I make this the next time I plan to reduce the dried ingredients by 15-20% as the flavor is actually stronger than I would prefer (but this is very good as is). I bought a double pack of artichoke hearts at Sams with the idea of marinating on my own. The first batch of me winging it did not turn out, very happy to have found this recipe. Note - the Artichokes from Sams are quite tender, I recommend filling the container you are using with the plain artichokes and pour the marinating mixture over the top.
awesome....super simple...I chopped the artichoke hearts...great on pita wedges...or slices of grilled bread as a bruschetta topping...so easy...
